newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS CRUSHES AGASSI IN 57 MINUTES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS CRUSHES AGASSI IN 57 MINUTES.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras took just under an hour to crush his American compatriot Andre Agassi 6-4 6-1 in an extraordinary quarter-final at the Stuttgart Open on Friday.
After winning an unusual first set which saw seven breaks of serve, Sampras ran away with the second set to reach the semifinals after just 57 minutes.
Sampras and Agassi have clashed in three major grand slam finals -- the last in 1995 when Sampras won the U.S. Open in four sets.
Agassi, who needs some good results over the next few weeks to make sure of his place at next month's season-ending world championship, was a long way from his best.

After they both held their opening service games, there were seven breaks in the next eight games. Sampras, however, kept his nerve, clinching the first set after 36 minutes when Agassi hit a wide forehand.
Agassi, ranked ninth in the world, never fully recovered his composure as Sampras ran away to a 5-0 lead in the second set on his way to victory.
In Saturday's semifinals the three-times Wimbledon champion will meet Dutchman Jan Siemerink who beat Croatian fifth seed Goran Ivanisevic 6-3 7-6 in the first quarter-final of the day.
